intro: Iceland has fewer than 400,000 people, about two-thirds of them in and around Reykjavík, the world's most northerly capital.

chapters.title: Names and language
text: Icelanders usually take their father's or mother's first name plus -son or -dóttir as their surname, so people are listed by first name, even in the phone book. Icelandic has changed so little that Icelanders can still read the medieval sagas.
About a fifth of residents were born abroad, especially in Poland.

chapters.title: A nation of readers
text: Icelanders publish and buy huge numbers of books; giving books on Christmas Eve, the 'Christmas book flood', is a beloved tradition. Swimming pools are the heart of social life, and many people respect stories of hidden elves.

keyTerms.meaning: A surname formed from a parent's first name, like Jónsdóttir, 'Jón's daughter'.
